slides.head:
Tidal is banning fully AI-generated
music from its platform.
The ban starts December 9.
slides.body: On November 24, Tidal said on X it will reject and remove wholly AI-generated tracks, and bar distributors from delivering them. Tracks assisted by AI tools are still allowed.

slides.head: 43% of new deliveries.
slides.body: Tidal says 43% of all tracks distributed to it over the past 90 days were detected as wholly AI-generated. On November 6, it was over 60% of that day's deliveries.

slides.head: 27 million tracks, few listeners.
slides.body: About 27 million tracks on Tidal are tagged as AI, 6.3% of its catalog. Tidal says 96% of them received zero streams in the last three months.

slides.head: Most of it traces to Suno.
slides.body: Tidal says 94% of tracks carrying its AI badge are attributed to Suno. It has also taken down more than 65,000 AI tracks over suspected impersonation of artist names.

slides.head: The tool is fine. The output isn't.
slides.body: If AI helps you make the track, you stay. If AI is the whole track, it gets rejected. Watch if other platforms follow.
